title: Broccoli-shaped mallee eucalyptus (South Australia)
description: Eucalyptus socialis (red mallee) looks like a giant broccoli: round, dense foliage on short, multi-stemmed trunks. It is concentrated around Adelaide and the Murray Mallee, also on the Eyre and Yorke peninsulas and the mid-north, spreading into the mallee of north-western Victoria and south-western New South Wales.

title: King Island pastures
description: King Island (Bass Strait, Tasmania) shows large golden pastures full of cattle, lined with very tall, thin eucalyptus with white trunks.

title: Hoop pines (Queensland coast)
description: The hoop pine (Araucaria cunninghamii) is easy to recognise: often very tall, with pompom-like foliage clumps like the Paraná pine but reaching all the way down the trunk. It is very common around Brisbane and extends up the Queensland coast to Cape York.

title: 'Queensland label' pole tops on three outback roads
description: This pole top with a crossarm and supports above and below (picture the Queensland label in the middle) seems to be unique to three east–west roads in Queensland: the Flinders Highway between Julia Creek and Hughenden, the Landsborough/Capricorn Highway between Longreach and Barcaldine, and the Warrego Highway between Morven and Roma.

title: Southern Queensland pole tops
description: This pole top shape indicates southern Queensland, on a few specific roads: Quilpie–Cooladdi–Charleville, Charleville–Cunnamulla via Wyandra, Charleville–Mitchell–Roma, and Roma–Surat–St George–Dirranbandi.

title: River level gauges (mostly Queensland)
description: Staff gauges, the tall graduated boards that measure river water levels, can be found throughout Australia but are far more common in Queensland.

title: Canberra edge-line road reflectors
description: Raised reflectors placed on the outer edge line, cutting through it, indicate Canberra (ACT). If there is only a hole and no reflector, you are probably in South Australia, though this is less reliable.
